L26: > Abstract: Let $M(4,3)$ be the maximum size of a finite simple family of four-element sets containing no three distinct members whose pairwise intersections are equal. The empty intersection is included in the forbidden configurations. We give a computer-assisted exclusion of families of size $69$, giving the bound $54\le M(4,3)\le 68$. The argument combines an imported bound of $27$ for intersecting families, structural analysis of point-links, exact trace constraints and finite exhaustions.
L27: The proof is organized at the cardinality $69$. A cap on families containing a complete $R16$ point-link provides a shorter final contradiction. We make the imported results, computational lemma contracts and remaining verification limits explicit. The lower construction is classical. Neither exclusion of size $68$ nor optimality of the lower construction is claimed.
L28: Comments:  | 17 pages. Computer-assisted finite bound 54 <= M(4,3) <= 68, with empty kernels included; forcing threshold at most 69. Companion at public commit 90c03c79bcf44eb8f61dff1b86091b822cc4cd3c. The general sunflower conjecture and the exact value remain open.

L64: ### Process summary
L65: The author studied the finite extremal problem for three-sunflower-free families of four-element sets. Generative AI tools assisted proof development, software preparation and manuscript review, as disclosed in the paper. The author reports using OpenAI Sol 5.6, Astra 6, Pro 6 and Sol 6.1; these model names are an author disclosure for this deposit, not model names quoted from the manuscript. No individual lemma is assigned to a particular model. The named human author is responsible for the claims.
L66: The argument excludes a hypothetical family of size 69. It imports the intersecting-family bound 27 from Axante et al., arXiv:2609.06175v1, Proposition 6.7. Structural point-link analysis and exact trace constraints reduce the maximum-degree possibilities. Jin's strict graph-homomorphism theorem, in the formulation of Nikiforov's Theorem A, then supplies a fibre decomposition. The remaining case forces a complete R16 point-link; a separate local cap of 61 contradicts size 69.
L67: The classical 54-member lower construction is reproduced for context. The local cap is not a global bound of 61.
L68: This is a high-level account of the method and division of labour. The deposit includes the manuscript and its LaTeX source and links the computational companion; no raw conversations or agent-session files are attached.
L69: ### Verification
L70: On 9 October 2026, a fresh complete replay from an isolated copy of public commit 90c03c79bcf44eb8f61dff1b86091b822cc4cd3c passed all 42 finite verification suites in normal and optimized Python: 84 successful executions, with identical semantic results in all 42 pairs. The final wrapper and repository-integrity checks passed. Auxiliary and adverse-input tests produced 66 successful test executions and two skips for a Windows symlink/junction privilege requirement.
L71: Initial temporary-directory permission failures were retained and the affected tests passed with an explicit writable directory; no source patch was needed.
L72: An isolated three-pass build produced the same text and rendered pixels on all 17 pages as the public PDF. The distributed PDF and manuscript source are unchanged. Two Sol 6.1 agents and the primary agent reviewed the proof interfaces, source statements and claim boundaries; the agents shared project material and communicated. Several small domains were reconstructed separately from definitions without importing repository code.
L73: These are author-side computational checks and AI reviews, not independent specialist endorsement or end-to-end formal verification. The external intersecting-family theorem H27 is imported from Axante et al., arXiv:2609.06175v1, Proposition 6.7; its original exhaustive search is not rerun here. No exhaustive priority certification is claimed.
L74: ### Negative results & failed approaches
L75: The manuscript does not exclude a family of size 68, determine the exact value M(4,3), or prove optimality of the classical 54-member construction. It does not resolve the general Erdős-Rado sunflower conjecture (Erdős Problem #20). The comparison with the upper bound 83 is specifically with Axante et al., arXiv:2609.06175v1, Theorem 6.9; no exhaustive priority claim is made. The original external H27 exhaustive computation is not rerun by this companion.
L76: No independent specialist endorsement or end-to-end formal proof is supplied.
